item.title: Gambonanza Gambit Chaining Guide - Stack Triggers in One Turn
item.description:
Chaining 101

One Gambit per turn is fine. Three Gambits on one capture wins games.

A chain is not a script. It is a board you build so that one move satisfies several Gambit trigger conditions at once.

See the All Gambits Guide for the full list, and the Deterministic Gambits Guide for the difference between guaranteed and chance-based triggers.

How Chaining Really Works

Every Gambit fires from a trigger condition. You do not “play” three Gambits in a row. Instead, you arrange the board so one action triggers several at once.

item.title: Gambonanza Gambit Combinations - How to Pick Gambits That Work Together
item.description:
Gambonanza Gambit Combinations - How to Pick Gambits That Work Together

Quick Fix

You can only hold five Gambits, so every slot counts. Pick combinations whose triggers fire on the same action:

Combination What lines them up Why it works
Tempo plus capture A capture that also skips the enemy turn You take a piece and keep the initiative
Pawn payout stack Pawn moves and pawn captures Several payouts on the same pawn action
Landing plus payout A landing you had to make anyway The turn earns twice
Queen support A surviving queen plus capture payouts Your best piece both earns and carries
Boss-answer flex The boss preview plus one swap You always have the right tool for the modifier

How to Build a Combination

Rule 1: Start from a trigger, not a name

item.title: Gambonanza Gambit Chain Broke? 4 Ways to Salvage the Run
item.description:
Gambit Chain Broken \u2014 TL;DR Check All Gambits Guide for the full breakdown. The Combo Chain Guide breaks this down in detail.

Don\u2019t panic. Don\u2019t restart.

A broken chain is recoverable in 2\u20133 moves if you know your fallback routes. The most common fix: insert a neutral Gambit (King\u2019s Pawn / Knight\u2019s Pawn) to reset the chain state, then pivot into a secondary chain.

item.title: Your Combo Loop Backfired? How to Spot Self-Destructive Gambit Cycles Before They Wipe Your Run
item.description:
You built the infinite loop. Endless value. Unlimited economy. Everything was working. Then your gold hit zero in three turns.

I see this pattern in community run logs every week. A player discovers a gambit loop that produces endless triggers. They think they have won. But the loop has a hidden cost structure that drains their economy faster than it generates. By the time they notice, the board is full of worthless summons, their gold is empty, and the AI is one move away from wiping the board.
